fact.thing: yearly coupon cap on a BMO NVIDIA-linked autocallable note
fact.box: BMO NVIDIA-linked autocallable note (US 424B2, January 2026), not the NVIA ETF
fact.claim: In a January 2026 BMO note linked to NVIDIA, the most you could earn was a coupon of about 17.75% a year, no matter how much NVIDIA rose. The coupon was paid only in quarters when NVIDIA closed at or above 70% of its starting price, and the note was redeemed early if NVIDIA closed above 100% of that price. If NVIDIA was below the 70% trigger at maturity, the holder could lose some or all of their principal. These are the terms of a single BMO note, not of the new NVIA ETF, which has not published its own figures on any page we could open.

felt.how: the most $10,000 in the note pays in a full year (4 × $443.75), even if NVIDIA doubles

sources.label: BMO 424B2 PRICING SUPPLEMENT (SEC)
sources.what: The notes will pay a Contingent Coupon on each Contingent Coupon Payment Date at the Contingent Interest Rate of 4.4375% per quarter (approximately 17.75% per annum) if the closing level of the Reference Asset on the applicable quarterly Observation Date is greater than or equal to its Coupon Barrier Level.

sources.label: BMO 424B2 PRICING SUPPLEMENT (SEC)
sources.what: Your return on the notes is limited to the Contingent Coupons, if any, regardless of any appreciation in the value of the Reference Asset.

sources.label: BMO NEWSROOM
sources.what: The BMO ETFs invest in Autocallable Transactions which are derivatives that expose investors to downside risk.

This note pays you at most about 17.75% a year, no matter how high NVIDIA climbs, and it only pays in a quarter when NVIDIA closes at or above 70% of where it started.

plain.do: Write down two numbers from any note like this: the yearly cap and the price line where the payments stop.
